response: No, the WHO/UNAIDS/UNICEF-recommended replacement milks for infants of HIV-infected mothers are not entirely appropriate in the South African context. According to the available data, no home-prepared replacement milks in South Africa meet all the estimated micronutrient and essential fatty acid requirements of infants under 6 months. The only replacement milk that meets all nutritional needs is commercial infant formula. To provide total nutrition, replacement milks should include additional ingredients such as vegetable oils (like soybean oil) as a source of linoleic and alpha-linolenic acids, as well as extra vitamins and minerals. Revisions to the WHO/UNAIDS/UNICEF HIV and infant feeding course replacement milk options are necessary to address this issue.
